kernel: the verify lane table (split-K, msg, matmul2d, NAX m16, crossrow)
summary: vqmmLaneForTile picks one of five custom verify-width affine quantized-matmul lanes per call from M, K, N and the machine's tile class, and the qmatmul front door tries it after the format engines, the row-exact kernels and lane_qmm, before the prefill dequant GEMM and stock mlx_quantized_matmul. Split-K serves M 2..7 (a threadgroup owns 4 output columns, 2 at M=7; K splits over 2 simdgroups at N >= 4096 else 4; one barrier; fp32 accumulation), the wide msg tile serves M 2..7 at N >= 100000 with 8 simdgroups and no barrier, the matmul2d tile serves M 8..16 on M5 matrix units and M 8..24 as plain shader code on applegpu_g16 under macOS 26.2+, and a 4-bit g64 crossrow lane for M 8..9 ships opt-in-off after a measured 4% loss. M=1 and M past the tile caps stay on stock qmv/qmm_splitk.

gates.condition: front door Transformer.qmatmul arm order: GGUF kernels first, then sushi row-scaled fp8, then (when a Hadamard rotation registry or ternary pack is bound) qmv_nax2 before qmv2 plus opt-in int8, then rowExactQmm, then qmatmulBits; each custom arm returns null to decline and the caller keeps going
gates.note: gguf at 19312, fp8 at 19313, Hadamard/ternary at 19321-19342, row-exact at 19343-19345, qmatmulBits at 19346

gates.condition: qmatmulBits affine tail order: lane_qmm.tiledQmm (a weight re-tiled at drafter bind, NAX), then a plain matmul for null-scale bf16 weights, then non-affine mxfp arms, then simdQmmDecode (biases present), then verifyQmm, then qmv_cuda, then prefillDqGemm, then stock mlx_quantized_matmul, which is where every one-row dense decode projection lands
gates.note: lane_qmm at 44981, bf16 at 44986, simdQmmDecode at 45020, prefillDqGemm at 45066, stock at 45070

gates.condition: rowExactDecode = row_exact_covered and dflash_bound and rowExactArch: only where every projection fits the row kernels and a DFlash drafter is bound; dense qwen3_5 (non-MoE, hadamard_block == 0) or nemotron_h. It replaces the lanes above when it holds; serial and MTP keep the faster stock paths otherwise
gates.note: rowExactArch at src/model.zig:1235-1238; the pick (lane_qmm on NAX hosts, then simd_qmm, rowqmv fallback) at src/transformer.zig:36692-36697

gates.condition: vqmmLaneForTile selection order: M outside 2..max_m declines; N < 512 declines; the nax/shader tile wins first (M >= tile_min_m and K % 256 == 0 and N % 32 == 0); then M > 16 declines; then M > 7 takes crossrow when opted in (M <= 9, K % 512, N % 8, N >= 1024) or none; then K % 64 and N % 4 gate; finally N >= 100000 picks msg, else splitk
gates.note: body at src/transformer.zig:2130-2144; tile_min_m is 8 for the shader tile and nax_min_m (default 8, q8 7) otherwise

gates.condition: verifyQmm entry gates: GPU stream, bits in 4/5/6/8, group size in 32/64/128, scales and biases present, x bfloat16 or float16, packed geometry w_cols * 32 == K * bits
gates.note: bits at 2166, gs at 2167, dtypes at 2170, geometry at 2181

gates.condition: plain-SIMD mixed widths: mixedPlainShapeEnabled (4-bit true; 5/6-bit at gs 64/128 needs N >= 2560; 8-bit false); MLX_SERVE_VERIFY_QMM_MIXED_PLAIN 0/1 forces the A/B arms
gates.note: env mode parse at src/transformer.zig:2064-2074, application at 2084-2091

gates.condition: NAX mixed widths: naxMixedBitsEnvEnabled (MLX_SERVE_VERIFY_QMM_NAX_MIXED=0 disables without touching q4 NAX) and mixedNaxShapeEnabled (gs64 N >= 5120 for q5/q6/q8, or gs 64/128 N >= 2560 with M > 8 for q5/q6)
gates.note: shape gate at src/transformer.zig:2009-2015, env at 2585-2594

gates.condition: NAX availability: not force-fallback, G17-class GPU, macOS >= 26.2; the kernel object is NEVER BUILT, not just never dispatched, where the probe is false (matmul2d pipeline creation can fail off-G17)

split-K lane live on DFlash; about 0 on serial decode
whole-forward estimate at M=5 for K_PARTS = 1, 2, 4, 8; shipped 2 is optimal
measured.note: same A/B in the kernel comment at src/transformer.zig:1774-1776

measured.conditions: isolated microbench at M=4 versus stock at huge N; in context at regular N the split-K lane is their winner over the wide tile, and the tile holds 1.18x off the weight-stream floor per their source ledger

measured.conditions: MTP on, decode tok/s from the server's own timings, per-prompt medians over two passes with cell order reversed (the first cell of a pass reads about 2% fast); forcing every shape on measured only 1.01-1.05x, and killing the 4-bit lane outright on the same box costs 1.09-1.12x, so the 6-bit lane is worth more than the 4-bit one it was modelled on; 8-bit ships off, 5-bit unmeasured and off
measured.note: table at src/transformer.zig:2030-2033, force-all at 2045-2047, 4-bit-lane kill at 2035-2037

measured.conditions: forced depth 8, six paired thermally-settled counterbalanced boots, identical 885/888 acceptance, NAX engagement present in every ON log and absent in every OFF log

four concurrent streams with the matmul2d shader tile serving rows past 7 (8/16/24-row tiles at 11.2 TFLOP/s; whole-forward qmm 62.6 / 73.3 / 104.3 ms against stock 84.7 / 133 / 134; a 32-row tile exceeds threadgroup memory and stock runs 12.2 TFLOP/s there); Inco Splash measured 94.6 aggregate on the same box; greedy; the whole entry is flagged N=1 upstream and still holds by their re-test

S=16 marginal 89.4 - 33.7 = 55.7 ms decomposed with the batched microbench summed over the pack inventory: qmm 35.5 ms at M=1 (the entire serial forward) and 73.8 ms at M=16, 11.1 TFLOP/s, about 70% of the M4 Max fp32 peak; the GDN recurrence is not in the marginal (12.3 ms at T=1, 8.7 at T=16, negative marginal); the remaining 19 ms is attention and glue

same-boot forced-depth-8 echo A/B; it won in the origin stack because their host dispatched M independent qmv columns so pairing rows halved weight reads, while here M 8/9 fall to stock mlx_quantized_matmul whose gemm tile already reads each weight once; ships opt-in-off, adoption predicate admits no shape by default

measured.value: 5-8% slower at every width (M=5: 45.9 vs 43.0 ms whole-forward)
measured.conditions: bn=8 versus bn=4 at M 2..5; the activation-traffic arithmetic predicted a near-halving of the dominant read, but the x rows are 66 KB and never left cache, so the extra accumulators only cost occupancy; kept behind MLX_SERVE_VQMM_BN
measured.note: same disproof in the kernel comment at src/transformer.zig:1762-1769

measured.conditions: T(7) round with the split-K tile extended to M=8 at bn=4 versus stock; spill/occupancy past 7 live Vec8 row vectors, so plain-SIMD eligibility caps at M=7
the array-indexed Vec8 v[MROWS] form of the same kernel at M=6, exactly as the upstream design ledger warned; the shipped form emits named scalars with literal accumulator indices
the standing NAX min-M sweep at M = 5, 6, 7 relative to the plain lane; q4/q6 retain M=8 while q8 defaults to M=7, so one family-wide minimum would regress at least two measured widths
their quality-per-byte comparison; the reason the 6-bit lane was worth building even though it is not the primary pack

TURBOSPARK_INT4_MMA8: our 8-row-flat INT4 MMA verify surface (crates/runtime/src/real_forward_dispatch.rs:344, default off, MAX_ROWS 8 at crates/gpu/src/dequant_int4_mma8.rs:20, min-rows override TURBOSPARK_INT4_MMA8_MIN_ROWS), used as the flat-verify arm by crates/lab/src/depth_replay.rs:81; the A/B against this lane table is row-band against row-band

notes: Doc-vs-source conflicts, sided with the source. (1) Our split-K table row says the 5/6/8-bit forms are shape-gated to N >= 5120; the source's plain-SIMD (split-K/msg) mixed adoption floor is MIXED_PLAIN_MIN_N = 2560 for 5/6-bit at gs 64/128, and 8-bit ships off entirely on the plain lanes (src/transformer.zig:2052-2060). N >= 5120 is the NAX tile's g64 wide gate (mixedNaxShapeEnabled, src/transformer.zig:2011), which our doc's table attached to the wrong lane. (2) Our doc says forcing every shape on measured 1.03 to 1.05x; the source says 1.01-1.05x (src/transformer.zig:2047). (3) Our doc quotes the 27B ladder S=8 = 61.3 ms without the upstream caveat that it was measured with an experimental sg8 lane serving M 8..16 that has since been reverted; without it S=8 is 89.6 ms (docs/gotchas/engine-mlx.md:222), and an earlier all-stock 27B ladder reads S=2..8 = 34.9/36.0/39.5/44.8/49.9/89.6 ms (docs/gotchas/engine-mlx.md:4544). (4) get_qmv_batch_limit lives in MLX's quantized.cpp, not this repo; the (10 on these shapes) crossover figure is their prose repeated in docs/gotchas/engine-mlx.md:2179-2181 and src/transformer.zig:59190-59193, while the in-repo mirror qmvBatchLimit for the joined path reads 33/25/13 single-die and 32/18/12 dual-die on gen-17 (src/transformer.zig:44961-44965) and does not read 10 on the 27B shapes. (5) The upstream doc names the ladder model a 4-bit Muse trunk (docs/gotchas/engine-mlx.md:2172); the Muse-Glimmer 30B name comes from the model sources (src/muse_vision.zig:797), so our doc's model name is an inference from the tree, not their ladder text. Other caveats. The msg tile's 2.1x is isolated at lm-head-class N; the source also records it at 1.18x off the weight-stream floor and names split-K their in-context winner at regular N. The shader tile is the same NAX m16 kernel source compiled as plain shader on gen-16 with the row height as the BMT template arg, so 11.2 TFLOP/s is a shader-code number, not the M5 units. NAX availability needs generation >= 17 (phone floor 18) AND macOS >= 26.2, and the kernel object is never built off the probe. The crossrow lane is reachable only where the tile branch declines and stays opt-in-off after its 4% loss. Activation dtype for every lane is bf16 or fp16 only. benchmarks.md's release rows for Qwen3.8 27B 4-bit dflash (109 tok/s at 26.10.2, 106 at 26.10.3, M4 Max) are release table cells, not lane A/Bs.
